Cedar Hollow Tile (V-109) gave a W-9 with the business name on line 1 and an SSN as a sole proprietor; IRS TIN Matching found no match. Form W-9 asks a sole proprietor for the owner's name on line 1 and the business name on line 2. The draft reports $26,850.00 under the name and TIN on file. A person gets the corrected W-9 before filing; filed as is, the form is likely to draw an IRS notice and a B notice, after which backup withholding would apply.

Ridgeline Concrete Cutting (V-108) never gave a W-9 or a TIN. 24% backup withholding was due on all 5 payments, $3,456.00; accounts payable withheld $2,112.00 from April 30 on, reported in box 4. The $1,344.00 not withheld from February 27 and March 31 is HANGS's own liability. A person reports the backup withholding on Form 945 and keeps soliciting the TIN; the form is filed with the TIN box blank.

Tomas Arvelo, an individual, was paid $33,348.00 through accounts payable in 2026 for 794 hours of concrete finishing at $42.00 an hour under the HGC foreman, the question left open by the Q3 Form 941 review. The draft reports a Form 1099-NEC as accounts payable recorded the work. If a person decides the work is employment, the pay belongs on a Form W-2 with withholding instead, and the payroll returns change.

Two payees belong on Form 1099-MISC, which this run does not prepare: $96,000.00 of office rent to Harbor Ridge Office Partners LLC (box 1), and the $85,000.00 settlement paid to Moss and Tarrant PLLC (box 10, gross proceeds paid to an attorney). Form 1099-MISC has its own dates: e-filed with the IRS by March 31, 2027.

Unsigned draft. The 9 Forms 1099-NEC are due to the IRS and to the recipients by Monday, February 1, 2027 (January 31 is a Sunday). HANGS must e-file; no Form 1096 is filed with an electronic filing.
